candidates.name: Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley
candidates.reason: UNESCO glacial valley — Andorra la Vella's headline nature/culture crossover pick — but neither the official valley site nor secondary sources confirm November trail/access conditions at altitude. For a first-time-Pyrenees, moderate-walker party, shipping it without a confirmed access window risks sending them into snow-affected terrain. Flagged for Pass A/reconcile to verify closer to the trip rather than shipped here.

candidates.name: Naturlandia
candidates.reason: The park's own site confirms a weekends-only autumn schedule before the winter toboggan/zipline season opens, but the winter opening has historically landed around 29 Nov (last cycle) — after this trip's 5–9 Nov window — and the exact 2026 autumn-weekend calendar couldn't be pinned to a primary source. Recommending it risks sending the party to a closed or partially-closed park; last year's date is a lead, not a confirmed 2026 date.

candidates.name: Caldea
candidates.reason: Doesn't map cleanly to the stated culture/food/nature priorities, and the resident/experiential angle (low-season weekday mornings are quieter) only reached aggregator-tier sourcing after two firsthand-review fetches (tripbytrip.org, actividadesenandorra.com's ex-employee guide) were blocked with 403s. Not solid enough to ship on its own; reconcile may still want a one-line crowd-timing note if Pass A carries Caldea as a marquee sight.

candidates.name: Celler d'en Toni
candidates.reason: Established since 1964 and Michelin-Guide-listed, but firsthand reviews single out the wine list and overall price-to-quality ratio as weak points. MiraKbé and Borda Estevet cover the same 'worth-seeking-out traditional Andorran food' niche at better value for this mid-range-budget pair.

candidates.name: El Crostó
candidates.reason: Intimate 8-table Catalan fine-dining spot, well-reviewed, but sourcing stayed aggregator-tier (no independent firsthand account found within budget) and it likely sits above the stated $75–150/day mid-range budget as an everyday pick. Flagging as a possible single splurge night for reconcile rather than shipping outright.

candidates.name: Bar-Restaurant La Sardana
candidates.reason: Surfaced only via a single aggregator listicle mention, with no independent second source found within budget. One uncorroborated aggregator mention doesn't clear the experiential corroboration bar, so omitted rather than shipped on thin sourcing.

evidence.claim: Casa de la Vall (Andorra's historic 16th-century parliament house, Barri Antic) is open Nov–Apr 10:00–14:00 & 15:00–18:00, closed Sundays and Mondays; admission is by reservation only via +376 839760 or museusandorra@gmail.com — no walk-up visits. Standard admission €5, concessions €2.50.

Church of Santa Coloma (Andorra la Vella's oldest church, 8th–9th c. nave with a unique 12th-c. circular Lombard bell tower) is open Jan–May & Oct–Dec 10:00–14:00 & 15:00–18:00, closed Sun/Mon; €7 standard admission. Unlike Casa de la Vall, self-guided audioguide visits do NOT require advance reservation — only the guided-tour option does (book via +376 839760 / reservesmuseus@govern.ad).

MiraKbé gastrobar (Carrer Pere d'Urg 10, Andorra la Vella) runs a weekday lunch set-menu Mon–Fri 13:00–15:15 (€12, incl. water/wine/beer) and an à la carte tapas dinner service; phone/floor service runs 10:00–16:00 & 19:00–23:00 Mon–Sat, closed Sundays.

MiraKbé is a resident-food-blog pick precisely for sitting off Andorra la Vella's touristy main shopping street — the blog names it the one restaurant it specifically recommends inside the capital after multiple repeat visits, while warning that the main street's restaurants are 'usually overpriced' with lower-quality food.

A second, independent diner's account matches the same read: went for the weekday lunch menu, liked it enough to return the same trip for evening tapas, calling it 'obligatorio si estáis por Andorra' (a must if you're in Andorra).

Borda Estevet (traditional Andorran mountain-grill restaurant, Andorra la Vella) takes bookings via its own online form, phone (+376 864 026), or WhatsApp; lunch service runs 13:00–16:00, dinner 20:00–23:00. No deposit, cancellation, or walk-in policy is stated on the page itself.

The official Llac d'Engolasters hiking route (starting in Encamp, in front of the Automobile Museum) is 1.9 km, +350/-45 m elevation, rated Easy, roughly a 2-hour round trip (1h15 out, 45 min back) — a good fit for moderate walkers on a first Pyrenees trip without a full mountain-day commitment.
The Roc del Quer viewpoint / Tibetan bridge (operated by Pont Tibetà Canillo) posts hours of 9:30–19:00 daily (Mon–Fri and Sat–Sun alike), with no seasonal closure stated on the operator's own page.
Andorra's official tourism board describes Roc del Quer as remaining open year-round, Monday to Sunday, paid access, 'weather permitting' — i.e. no fixed seasonal closing date.

Catalan is Andorra's sole official language (Constitution of 1993). 2022 survey data: Catalan is the habitual language for 63.7% of the population, Spanish for 48.6%, Portuguese 6.6%, French 5.7% (respondents can name more than one) — Spanish, Portuguese and French usage stems mainly from Spanish/Portuguese immigration and from French/Spanish tourism; only Catalan is native to Andorra.

The EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) became fully operational on 10 April 2026 across all Schengen external border-crossing points, including land borders. It applies to non-EU short-stay visitors (e.g. US passport holders) and captures facial image, fingerprints, and travel-document data. This is a live, active change from the pre-2026 baseline a generic guide would assume for crossing into Andorra.

Direct Bus's Barcelona–El Prat Airport → Andorra la Vella coach runs 7 daily departures per terminal (T1: 07:30, 11:00, 13:00, 15:00, 17:30, 20:00, 23:00; T2: +15 min each), arriving in Andorra after approximately 3h30; passengers should arrive 30 min before departure; service runs 365 days/year.

reservations.walkIn: No walk-ins — admission is reservation-only (call +376 839760 or email museusandorra@gmail.com); book before arriving in Andorra la Vella, not on the day.
reservations.alternatives: Església de Santa Coloma, whose self-guided audioguide visit needs no advance reservation, if Casa de la Vall's limited slots don't line up with the trip.

reservations.walkIn: No explicit walk-in policy stated on the restaurant's own reservations page — book via the online form, phone, or WhatsApp rather than assuming a table will be free on arrival.
reservations.alternatives: MiraKbé (gastrobar, off the main tourist street) as a lower-key traditional-leaning alternative if Borda Estevet is booked out.

reservations.walkIn: Small room — reservations advised for the Wed–Sat tapas dinner service (+376 863 444 / +376 636 444 / reservesmirakbe@mkbgrup.com); the weekday lunch set-menu is more walk-in-friendly.

transport.route: Barcelona–El Prat / Girona / Toulouse–Blagnac airport → Andorra la Vella by scheduled coach (no rail option exists)
transport.doorToDoor: Direct Bus's own schedule (fetched) puts Barcelona–El Prat T1/T2 → Andorra la Vella at about 3h30 on its 7-daily-departure timetable (07:30/07:45 through 23:00/23:15 by terminal).
transport.transferReality: Andorra is not in the Schengen area, so this coach crosses an EU external Schengen border by land. As of 10 April 2026 the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) is fully operational and captures facial image + fingerprints from non-EU short-stay visitors (US passport holders included) at Schengen external border-crossing points, land borders included (European Commission, fetched) — a real change from the pre-2026 'no checks crossing into Andorra' baseline a generic guide would assume.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: Party of 2 moderate walkers with standard luggage — not a load factor on a scheduled coach with underfloor luggage holds.
transport.buffer: Andorran press (Alto.ad, fetched, published 5 Apr 2026) reports Andorra secured 'random' rather than 'systematic' EES checks specifically at the Spain/France land border to avoid stopping every vehicle, but also that EES lanes have caused delays of up to ~90 minutes at airports since Oct 2025 — the airport leg of this trip (the party's first Schengen entry) is the more likely delay point, not the coach's Andorra-side crossing.
transport.missedConnection: 7 daily departures per direction on the Direct Bus timetable alone (plus a separate Andbus/Novatel service) make a missed departure recoverable the same day.
transport.nextService: ~2h15–2h30 gaps between Direct Bus's own scheduled Barcelona-Airport departures.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: Last Direct Bus from Barcelona Airport to Andorra la Vella departs 23:00 (T1) / 23:15 (T2) per its own schedule.
transport.fallback: Andbus (Novatel) runs a parallel BCN-airport shuttle; taxi/private transfer is available at a higher price if a bus is missed.

disagreements.topic: Whether short-stay tourists (non-resident, non-EU passport) crossing the Andorra–Spain/France land border are covered by Andorra's EU border-management carve-out, or remain subject to full EES registration like any other Schengen external-border crossing
disagreements.investigation: The EU Commission's own EES page (fetched) states the system applies broadly to non-EU short-stay visitors at all Schengen external border-crossing points, land borders included, with no Andorra-specific carve-out mentioned. Andorran press (Alto.ad — fetched; digitalandorra.com, elperiodic.ad, laciutat.cat — search-preview, Catalan-language) describes a Govern d'Andorra–EU Border Management Agreement, but its exemption from EES registration is explicitly scoped to third-country nationals holding ANDORRAN RESIDENCY permits, not short-stay tourists; the same coverage separately reports Andorra secured 'random' rather than 'systematic' vehicle checks at the land border to avoid a traffic collapse. The two threads (resident exemption vs. random-vs-systematic checks) get conflated in some headlines.
disagreements.resolution: Unresolved in this pass — treat the party as subject to EES biometric registration at some point on this trip (most likely on arrival at the Barcelona/Toulouse/Girona airport, since that is their first Schengen external-border crossing); the Andorra land-border crossing itself is described as spot-check rather than universal, but that could change as the bilateral agreement's implementation proceeds through 2026. Reconcile should re-check govern.ad's own EES guidance page directly — attempted here but the fetch returned only nav-menu content, not the substantive text — closer to the trip date.

disagreements.topic: Whether Roc del Quer viewpoint / Tibetan bridge might close in November for weather/safety reasons
disagreements.investigation: The viewpoint's own operator page (ponttibetacanillo.com, fetched) and the official visitandorra.com page (fetched) both describe it as open on a regular daily schedule 'weather permitting' with no stated seasonal closure window. A third-party travel blog (estiber.com, fetched) instead states the site 'puede cerrarse en invierno por motivos de seguridad' (may close in winter for safety reasons), without citing a specific date range.
disagreements.resolution: Treated as low risk for a 5–9 Nov visit (early in the season, ahead of the heaviest typical snow), but not fully resolved. The guide should note it as a same-week check rather than assume it's guaranteed open, given the one blog's caveat against two official-tier sources saying otherwise.

saturation.note: Food and nature/outdoors searches converged on the same aggregator listicles (Wanderlog, Tripadvisor top-10s) by the last few rounds, and several individual review/blog pages (Tripadvisor review permalinks, tripbytrip.org, actividadesenandorra.com's ex-employee Caldea guide) returned 403s rather than new material. The one open thread — whether short-stay US-passport tourists get any EES carve-out at the Andorra land border — is recorded as a disagreement for reconcile rather than a reason to keep searching, since it changes a logistics buffer note, not which candidates ship.

nativeLanguage.why: English-language results for Andorra la Vella skew almost entirely to aggregator listicles (Tripadvisor top-10s, Wanderlog, generic 'best restaurants' roundups) that repeat the same handful of names. Catalan/Spanish queries reached Andorran-domain sources English search never surfaced: the official museums/monuments sites (museus.ad, casadelavall.ad), Andorran regional press (Alto.ad, Bondia, El Periòdic d'Andorra, La Veu Lliure, laciutat.cat) covering the 2026 EU border/EES rollout, and Catalan hiking sites (rutespirineus.cat, visitandorra.com's own routes) for trail specifics.
